search_log: Searched “Edward Rutherfurd London novel excerpt first chapter,” “London Edward Rutherfurd point of view third person narrator,” and Google Books/excerpt variants.

Opened the Penguin Random House publisher and retail pages; the retail page exposed the authorized 54 BC prose excerpt, while the main product page offered a sample control and whole-book description.
Searched for interior passages using “Londinium Edward Rutherfurd excerpt” and located a licensed Virtualo Polish excerpt containing sustained Saxon-era narration across several focal characters.

Searched targeted combinations with “omniscient,” “third-person,” “narrator,” and “point of view”; results were mostly generic, irrelevant, or structural reviews rather than explicit whole-book POV analysis. The archived New York Times first-chapter page was blocked by robots.txt.
person_note: The Goodreads excerpts repeatedly show a nonparticipating historical narrator moving across eras, scenes, and characters, with broad temporal knowledge and access to characters’ inner lives. The official English opening and a licensed interior translation independently exhibit the same third-person method. First- and second-person forms in the quotes are dialogue or generic maxims, not autonomous narrative sections. No credible evidence of sustained first- or second-person base narration was found. The main limitation is the absence of an explicit whole-book POV statement, but the agreement of two Tier A passages from different sections with numerous quotes from widely separated historical episodes supports THIRD at high confidence.
